def unique_element(lst):
    """
    Check if the list contains exactly one distinct element.
    
    Args:
        lst (list of numbers): The input list
        
    Returns:
        bool: True if all elements are the same, False otherwise
    """
    # Handle empty or single-element lists as they trivially have only one distinct element
    if len(lst) <= 1:
        return True
    
    # Get unique elements and check if there's exactly one
    unique_elements = set(lst)
    
    return len(unique_elements) == 1


# Test cases
assert unique_element([1, 1, 1]) == True
print("Test passed!")

# Additional test cases for verification
assert unique_element([]) == True          # Empty list
assert unique_element([5]) == True         # Single element
assert unique_element([2, 3]) == False     # Two different elements
assert unique_element([4, 4, 6, 6]) == False # Multiple distinct elements
print("All tests passed!")

unique_Element = unique_element
